title: Clickhouse
description: Monitor Clickhouse with metrics and logs
overview:
### Monitor Clickhouse with FuseScope

Collect key Clickhouse metrics and view them with an out of the box dashboard.  

Collect and parse Clickhouse logs to populate timestamp, severity, and other log attributes for better querying and aggregation.

Collect clickhouse query logs from system.query_log table and view them in FuseScope

configuration.title: Prerequisites
configuration.instructions:
## Before You Begin  

To configure metrics and logs collection for a Clickhouse server, you need the following.

### Ensure Clickhouse server is prepared for monitoring

- **Ensure that the Clickhouse server is running a supported version**  
  Clickhouse versions v23 and newer are supported.  
  You can use the following SQL statement to determine server version  
  ```SQL
  SELECT version();
  ```

- **If collecting metrics, ensure that Clickhouse is configured to export prometheus metrics**
  If needed, please [configure Clickhouse to expose prometheus metrics](https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/operations/server-configuration-parameters/settings#prometheus).

- **If collecting query_log, ensure that there is a clickhouse user with required permissions**
  To create a monitoring user for clickhouse, you can run:
  ```SQL
  CREATE USER monitoring IDENTIFIED BY 'monitoring_password';
  GRANT SELECT ON system.query_log to monitoring;

  -- If monitoring a clustered deployment, also grant privilege for executing remote queries
  GRANT REMOTE ON *.* TO 'monitoring' on CLUSTER 'cluster_name';
  ```


### Ensure OTEL Collector is running and has access to the Clickhouse server

- **Ensure that an OTEL collector is running in your deployment environment**  
  If needed, please [install an OTEL Collector](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/collector/installation/)  
  If already installed, ensure that the collector version is v0.88.0 or newer.  
  If collecting logs from system.query_log table, ensure that the collector version is v0.88.23 or newer.

  Also ensure that you can provide config files to the collector and that you can set environment variables and command line flags used for running it.  

- **Ensure that the OTEL collector can access the Clickhouse server**  
  In order to collect metrics, the collector must be able to reach clickhouse server and access the port on which prometheus metrics are being exposed.

  In order to collect server logs, the collector must be able to read the Clickhouse server log file.

  In order to collect logs from query_log table, the collector must be able to reach the server and connect to it as a clickhouse user with required permissions.

configuration.title: Collect Metrics
configuration.instructions:
### Collect Clickhouse Metrics

You can configure Clickhouse metrics collection by providing the required collector config to your collector.

#### Create collector config file

Save the following config for collecting Clickhouse metrics in a file named `clickhouse-metrics-collection-config.yaml`

```yaml
receivers:
  prometheus/clickhouse:
    config:
      global:
        scrape_interval: 60s
      scrape_configs:
        - job_name: clickhouse
          static_configs:
            - targets:
                - ${env:CLICKHOUSE_PROM_METRICS_ENDPOINT}
          metrics_path: ${env:CLICKHOUSE_PROM_METRICS_PATH}

processors:
  # enriches the data with additional host information
  # see https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/processor/resourcedetectionprocessor#resource-detection-processor
  resourcedetection/system:
    # add additional detectors if needed
    detectors: ["system"]
    system:
      hostname_sources: ["os"]

exporters:
  otlp/fusescope:
    endpoint: ${env:OTLP_DESTINATION_ENDPOINT}
    tls:
      # set to false when the FuseScope endpoint uses TLS
      insecure: true

service:
  pipelines:
    metrics/clickhouse:
      receivers: [prometheus/clickhouse]
      # note: remove this processor if the collector host is not running on the same host as the clickhouse instance
      processors: [resourcedetection/system]
      exporters: [otlp/fusescope]
```

#### Set Environment Variables

Set the following environment variables in your otel-collector environment:

```bash
# Prometheus metrics endpoint on the clickhouse server reachable from the otel collector.
# You can examine clickhouse server configuration to find it. For details see https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/operations/server-configuration-parameters/settings#prometheus
export CLICKHOUSE_PROM_METRICS_ENDPOINT="clickhouse:9363"

# Prometheus metrics path on the clickhouse server
# You can examine clickhouse server configuration to find it. For details see https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/operations/server-configuration-parameters/settings#prometheus
export CLICKHOUSE_PROM_METRICS_PATH="/metrics"

# OTLP gRPC endpoint of your FuseScope collector, see https://fuseone-io.github.io/fusescope-docs/sending-data/otlp/
export OTLP_DESTINATION_ENDPOINT="<fusescope-otel-collector-host>:4317"

```

#### Use collector config file

Make the collector config file available to your otel collector and use it by adding the following flag to the command for running your collector  
```bash
--config clickhouse-metrics-collection-config.yaml
```  
Note: the collector can use multiple config files, specified by multiple occurrences of the --config flag.

configuration.title: Collect Server Logs
configuration.instructions:
### Collect Clickhouse Logs

You can configure Clickhouse logs collection by providing the required collector config to your collector.

#### Create collector config file

Save the following config for collecting clickhouse logs in a file named `clickhouse-logs-collection-config.yaml`

```yaml
receivers:
  filelog/clickhouse:
    include: ["${env:CLICKHOUSE_LOG_FILE}"]
    operators:
      # Parse default clickhouse text log format.
      # See https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/src/Loggers/OwnPatternFormatter.cpp
      - type: recombine
        source_identifier: attributes["log.file.name"]
        is_first_entry: body matches '^\\d{4}\\.\\d{2}\\.\\d{2}\\s+'
        combine_field: body
        overwrite_with: oldest
      - type: regex_parser
        parse_from: body
        if: body matches '^(?P<ts>\\d{4}\\.\\d{2}\\.\\d{2} \\d{2}:\\d{2}:\\d{2}.?[0-9]*)\\s+\\[\\s+(\\x1b.*?m)?(?P<thread_id>\\d*)(\\x1b.*?m)?\\s+\\]\\s+{((\\x1b.*?m)?(?P<query_id>[0-9a-zA-Z-_]*)(\\x1b.*?m)?)?}\\s+<(\\x1b.*?m)?(?P<log_level>\\w*)(\\x1b.*?m)?>\\s+((\\x1b.*?m)?(?P<clickhouse_component>[a-zA-Z0-9_]+)(\\x1b.*?m)?:)?\\s+(?s)(?P<message>.*)$'
        regex: '^(?P<ts>\d{4}\.\d{2}\.\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}.?[0-9]*)\s+\[\s+(\x1b.*?m)?(?P<thread_id>\d*)(\x1b.*?m)?\s+\]\s+{((\x1b.*?m)?(?P<query_id>[0-9a-zA-Z-_]*)(\x1b.*?m)?)?}\s+<(\x1b.*?m)?(?P<log_level>\w*)(\x1b.*?m)?>\s+((\x1b.*?m)?(?P<clickhouse_component>[a-zA-Z0-9_]+)(\x1b.*?m)?:)?\s+(?s)(?P<message>.*)$'
      - type: time_parser
        if: attributes.ts != nil
        parse_from: attributes.ts
        layout_type: gotime
        layout: 2006.01.02 15:04:05.999999
        location: ${env:CLICKHOUSE_TIMEZONE}
      - type: remove
        if: attributes.ts != nil
        field: attributes.ts
      - type: severity_parser
        if: attributes.log_level != nil
        parse_from: attributes.log_level
        overwrite_text: true
        # For mapping details, see getPriorityName defined in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/src/Interpreters/InternalTextLogsQueue.cpp
        mapping:
          trace:
            - Trace
            - Test
          debug: Debug
          info:
            - Information
            - Notice
          warn: Warning
          error: Error
          fatal:
            - Fatal
            - Critical
      - type: remove
        if: attributes.log_level != nil
        field: attributes.log_level
      - type: move
        if: attributes.message != nil
        from: attributes.message
        to: body
      - type: add
        field: attributes.source
        value: clickhouse

processors:
  batch:
    send_batch_size: 10000
    send_batch_max_size: 11000
    timeout: 10s

exporters:
  otlp/fusescope:
    endpoint: ${env:OTLP_DESTINATION_ENDPOINT}
    tls:
      # set to false when the FuseScope endpoint uses TLS
      insecure: true

service:
  pipelines:
    logs/clickhouse:
      receivers: [filelog/clickhouse]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [otlp/fusescope]
```

#### Set Environment Variables

Set the following environment variables in your otel-collector environment:

```bash

# path of Clickhouse server log file. must be accessible by the otel collector
# typically found at /var/log/clickhouse-server/clickhouse-server.log.
# Log file location can be found in clickhouse server config
# See https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/operations/server-configuration-parameters/settings#logger
export CLICKHOUSE_LOG_FILE="/var/log/clickhouse-server/server.log"

# Locale of the clickhouse server.
# Clickhouse logs timestamps in it's locale without TZ info
# Timezone setting can be found in clickhouse config. For details see https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/operations/server-configuration-parameters/settings#timezone
# Must be a IANA timezone name like Asia/Kolkata. For examples, see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones
export CLICKHOUSE_TIMEZONE="Etc/UTC"

# OTLP gRPC endpoint of your FuseScope collector, see https://fuseone-io.github.io/fusescope-docs/sending-data/otlp/
export OTLP_DESTINATION_ENDPOINT="<fusescope-otel-collector-host>:4317"

```

#### Use collector config file

Make the collector config file available to your otel collector and use it by adding the following flag to the command for running your collector  
```bash
--config clickhouse-logs-collection-config.yaml
```  
Note: the collector can use multiple config files, specified by multiple occurrences of the --config flag.

configuration.title: Collect Query Logs
configuration.instructions:
### Collect Clickhouse Query Logs

You can configure collection from system.query_log table in clickhouse by providing the required collector config to your collector.

> **Requires the FuseScope collector.** The `clickhousesystemtablesreceiver` used below ships only in [fusescope-otel-collector](https://github.com/fuseone-io/fusescope-otel-collector), not in `otelcol-contrib`.
> With `otelcol-contrib`, read `system.query_log` with the [`sqlquery` receiver](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/receiver/sqlqueryreceiver) instead, as a user that can `SELECT` on that table.

#### Create collector config file

Save the following config for collecting clickhouse query logs in a file named `clickhouse-query-logs-collection-config.yaml`

```yaml
receivers:
  clickhousesystemtablesreceiver/query_log:
    dsn: "${env:CLICKHOUSE_MONITORING_DSN}"
    cluster_name: "${env:CLICKHOUSE_CLUSTER_NAME}"
    query_log_scrape_config:
      scrape_interval_seconds: ${env:QUERY_LOG_SCRAPE_INTERVAL_SECONDS}
      min_scrape_delay_seconds: ${env:QUERY_LOG_SCRAPE_DELAY_SECONDS}

exporters:
  otlp/fusescope:
    endpoint: ${env:OTLP_DESTINATION_ENDPOINT}
    tls:
      # set to false when the FuseScope endpoint uses TLS
      insecure: true

service:
  pipelines:
    logs/clickhouse-query-logs:
      receivers: [clickhousesystemtablesreceiver/query_log]
      processors: []
      exporters: [otlp/fusescope]
```

#### Set Environment Variables

Set the following environment variables in your otel-collector environment:

```bash

# DSN for connecting to clickhouse with the monitoring user
# Replace monitoring:<PASSWORD> with `username:password` for your monitoring user
# Note: The monitoring user must be able to issue select queries on system.query_log table.
export CLICKHOUSE_MONITORING_DSN="tcp://monitoring:<PASSWORD>@clickhouse:9000/"

# If collecting query logs from a clustered deployment, specify a non-empty cluster name.
export CLICKHOUSE_CLUSTER_NAME=""

# Rows from query_log table will be collected periodically based on this setting
export QUERY_LOG_SCRAPE_INTERVAL_SECONDS=20

# Must be configured to a value greater than flush_interval_milliseconds setting for query_log.
# This setting can be found in the clickhouse server config
# For details see https://clickhouse.com/docs/en/operations/server-configuration-parameters/settings#query-log
# Setting a large enough value ensures all query logs for a particular time interval have been
# flushed before an attempt to collect them is made.
export QUERY_LOG_SCRAPE_DELAY_SECONDS=8

# OTLP gRPC endpoint of your FuseScope collector, see https://fuseone-io.github.io/fusescope-docs/sending-data/otlp/
export OTLP_DESTINATION_ENDPOINT="<fusescope-otel-collector-host>:4317"

```

#### Use collector config file

Make the collector config file available to your otel collector and use it by adding the following flag to the command for running your collector  
```bash
--config clickhouse-query-logs-collection-config.yaml
```
Note: the collector can use multiple config files, specified by multiple occurrences of the --config flag.

Also note that only 1 collector instance should be configured to collect query_logs.  
Using multiple collector instances or replicas with this config will lead to duplicate logs.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_Query
metrics.description: Number of queries to be interpreted and potentially executed. Does not include queries that failed to parse or were rejected due to AST size limits, quota limits or limits on the number of simultaneously running queries. May include internal queries initiated by ClickHouse itself. Does not count subqueries.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_SelectQuery
metrics.description: Same as Query, but only for SELECT queries.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_InsertQuery
metrics.description: Same as Query, but only for INSERT queries.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_QueriesWithSubqueries
metrics.description: Count queries with all subqueries

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_SelectQueriesWithSubqueries
metrics.description: Count SELECT queries with all subqueries

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_InsertQueriesWithSubqueries
metrics.description: Count INSERT queries with all subqueries

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_AsyncInsertQuery
metrics.description: Same as InsertQuery, but only for asynchronous INSERT queries.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_AsyncInsertBytes
metrics.description: Data size in bytes of asynchronous INSERT queries.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_AsyncInsertRows
metrics.description: Number of rows inserted by asynchronous INSERT queries.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_AsyncInsertCacheHits
metrics.description: Number of times a duplicate hash id has been found in asynchronous INSERT hash id cache.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_FailedQuery
metrics.description: Number of failed queries.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_FailedSelectQuery
metrics.description: Same as FailedQuery, but only for SELECT queries.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_FailedInsertQuery
metrics.description: Same as FailedQuery, but only for INSERT queries.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_FailedAsyncInsertQuery
metrics.description: Number of failed ASYNC INSERT queries.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_QueryTimeMicroseconds
metrics.description: Total time of all queries.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_SelectQueryTimeMicroseconds
metrics.description: Total time of SELECT queries.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_InsertQueryTimeMicroseconds
metrics.description: Total time of INSERT queries.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_OtherQueryTimeMicroseconds
metrics.description: Total time of queries that are not SELECT or INSERT.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_FileOpen
metrics.description: Number of files opened.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_Seek
metrics.description: Number of times the 'lseek' function was called.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_ReadBufferFromFileDescriptorRead
metrics.description: Number of reads (read/pread) from a file descriptor. Does not include sockets.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_ReadBufferFromFileDescriptorReadFailed
metrics.description: Number of times the read (read/pread) from a file descriptor have failed.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_ReadBufferFromFileDescriptorReadBytes
metrics.description: Number of bytes read from file descriptors. If the file is compressed, this will show the compressed data size.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_WriteBufferFromFileDescriptorWrite
metrics.description: Number of writes (write/pwrite) to a file descriptor. Does not include sockets.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_WriteBufferFromFileDescriptorWriteFailed
metrics.description: Number of times the write (write/pwrite) to a file descriptor have failed.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_WriteBufferFromFileDescriptorWriteBytes
metrics.description: Number of bytes written to file descriptors. If the file is compressed, this will show compressed data size.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_FileSync
metrics.description: Number of times the F_FULLFSYNC/fsync/fdatasync function was called for files.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_DirectorySync
metrics.description: Number of times the F_FULLFSYNC/fsync/fdatasync function was called for directories.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_FileSyncElapsedMicroseconds
metrics.description: Total time spent waiting for F_FULLFSYNC/fsync/fdatasync syscall for files.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_DirectorySyncElapsedMicroseconds
metrics.description: Total time spent waiting for F_FULLFSYNC/fsync/fdatasync syscall for directories.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_ReadCompressedBytes
metrics.description: Number of bytes (the number of bytes before decompression) read from compressed sources (files, network).

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_CompressedReadBufferBlocks
metrics.description: Number of compressed blocks (the blocks of data that are compressed independent of each other) read from compressed sources (files, network).

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_CompressedReadBufferBytes
metrics.description: Number of uncompressed bytes (the number of bytes after decompression) read from compressed sources (files, network).

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_UncompressedCacheHits
metrics.description: Number of times a block of data has been found in the uncompressed cache (and decompression was avoided).

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_UncompressedCacheMisses
metrics.description: Number of times a block of data has not been found in the uncompressed cache (and required decompression).

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_UncompressedCacheWeightLost
metrics.description: Number of bytes evicted from the uncompressed cache.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_MMappedFileCacheHits
metrics.description: Number of times a file has been found in the MMap cache (for the 'mmap' read_method), so we didn't have to mmap it again.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_MMappedFileCacheMisses
metrics.description: Number of times a file has not been found in the MMap cache (for the 'mmap' read_method), so we had to mmap it again.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_OpenedFileCacheHits
metrics.description: Number of times a file has been found in the opened file cache, so we didn't have to open it again.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_OpenedFileCacheMisses
metrics.description: Number of times a file has been found in the opened file cache, so we had to open it again.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_OpenedFileCacheMicroseconds
metrics.description: Amount of time spent executing OpenedFileCache methods.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_AIOWrite
metrics.description: Number of writes with Linux or FreeBSD AIO interface

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_AIOWriteBytes
metrics.description: Number of bytes written with Linux or FreeBSD AIO interface

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_AIORead
metrics.description: Number of reads with Linux or FreeBSD AIO interface

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_AIOReadBytes
metrics.description: Number of bytes read with Linux or FreeBSD AIO interface

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_IOBufferAllocs
metrics.description: Number of allocations of IO buffers (for ReadBuffer/WriteBuffer).

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_IOBufferAllocBytes
metrics.description: Number of bytes allocated for IO buffers (for ReadBuffer/WriteBuffer).

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_ArenaAllocChunks
metrics.description: Number of chunks allocated for memory Arena (used for GROUP BY and similar operations)

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_ArenaAllocBytes
metrics.description: Number of bytes allocated for memory Arena (used for GROUP BY and similar operations)

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_FunctionExecute
metrics.description: Number of SQL ordinary function calls (SQL functions are called on per-block basis, so this number represents the number of blocks).

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_TableFunctionExecute
metrics.description: Number of table function calls.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_MarkCacheHits
metrics.description: Number of times an entry has been found in the mark cache, so we didn't have to load a mark file.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_MarkCacheMisses
metrics.description: Number of times an entry has not been found in the mark cache, so we had to load a mark file in memory, which is a costly operation, adding to query latency.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_QueryCacheHits
metrics.description: Number of times a query result has been found in the query cache (and query computation was avoided). Only updated for SELECT queries with SETTING use_query_cache = 1.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_QueryCacheMisses
metrics.description: Number of times a query result has not been found in the query cache (and required query computation). Only updated for SELECT queries with SETTING use_query_cache = 1.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_CreatedReadBufferOrdinary
metrics.description: Number of times ordinary read buffer was created for reading data (while choosing among other read methods).

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_CreatedReadBufferDirectIO
metrics.description: Number of times a read buffer with O_DIRECT was created for reading data (while choosing among other read methods).

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_CreatedReadBufferDirectIOFailed
metrics.description: Number of times a read buffer with O_DIRECT was attempted to be created for reading data (while choosing among other read methods), but the OS did not allow it (due to lack of filesystem support or other reasons) and we fallen back to the ordinary reading method.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_CreatedReadBufferMMap
metrics.description: Number of times a read buffer using 'mmap' was created for reading data (while choosing among other read methods).

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_CreatedReadBufferMMapFailed
metrics.description: Number of times a read buffer with 'mmap' was attempted to be created for reading data (while choosing among other read methods), but the OS did not allow it (due to lack of filesystem support or other reasons) and we fallen back to the ordinary reading method.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_DiskReadElapsedMicroseconds
metrics.description: Total time spent waiting for read syscall. This include reads from page cache.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_DiskWriteElapsedMicroseconds
metrics.description: Total time spent waiting for write syscall. This include writes to page cache.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_NetworkReceiveElapsedMicroseconds
metrics.description: Total time spent waiting for data to receive or receiving data from network. Only ClickHouse-related network interaction is included, not by 3rd party libraries.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_NetworkSendElapsedMicroseconds
metrics.description: Total time spent waiting for data to send to network or sending data to network. Only ClickHouse-related network interaction is included, not by 3rd party libraries.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_NetworkReceiveBytes
metrics.description: Total number of bytes received from network. Only ClickHouse-related network interaction is included, not by 3rd party libraries.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_NetworkSendBytes
metrics.description: Total number of bytes send to network. Only ClickHouse-related network interaction is included, not by 3rd party libraries.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_DiskS3GetRequestThrottlerCount
metrics.description: Number of DiskS3 GET and SELECT requests passed through throttler.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_DiskS3GetRequestThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
metrics.description: Total time a query was sleeping to conform DiskS3 GET and SELECT request throttling.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_DiskS3PutRequestThrottlerCount
metrics.description: Number of DiskS3 PUT, COPY, POST and LIST requests passed through throttler.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_DiskS3PutRequestThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
metrics.description: Total time a query was sleeping to conform DiskS3 PUT, COPY, POST and LIST request throttling.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_S3GetRequestThrottlerCount
metrics.description: Number of S3 GET and SELECT requests passed through throttler.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_S3GetRequestThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
metrics.description: Total time a query was sleeping to conform S3 GET and SELECT request throttling.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_S3PutRequestThrottlerCount
metrics.description: Number of S3 PUT, COPY, POST and LIST requests passed through throttler.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_S3PutRequestThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
metrics.description: Total time a query was sleeping to conform S3 PUT, COPY, POST and LIST request throttling.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_RemoteReadThrottlerBytes
metrics.description: Bytes passed through 'max_remote_read_network_bandwidth_for_server'/'max_remote_read_network_bandwidth' throttler.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_RemoteReadThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
metrics.description: Total time a query was sleeping to conform 'max_remote_read_network_bandwidth_for_server'/'max_remote_read_network_bandwidth' throttling.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_RemoteWriteThrottlerBytes
metrics.description: Bytes passed through 'max_remote_write_network_bandwidth_for_server'/'max_remote_write_network_bandwidth' throttler.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_RemoteWriteThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
metrics.description: Total time a query was sleeping to conform 'max_remote_write_network_bandwidth_for_server'/'max_remote_write_network_bandwidth' throttling.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_LocalReadThrottlerBytes
metrics.description: Bytes passed through 'max_local_read_bandwidth_for_server'/'max_local_read_bandwidth' throttler.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_LocalReadThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
metrics.description: Total time a query was sleeping to conform 'max_local_read_bandwidth_for_server'/'max_local_read_bandwidth' throttling.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_LocalWriteThrottlerBytes
metrics.description: Bytes passed through 'max_local_write_bandwidth_for_server'/'max_local_write_bandwidth' throttler.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_LocalWriteThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
metrics.description: Total time a query was sleeping to conform 'max_local_write_bandwidth_for_server'/'max_local_write_bandwidth' throttling.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_ThrottlerSleepMicroseconds
metrics.description: Total time a query was sleeping to conform all throttling settings.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_QueryMaskingRulesMatch
metrics.description: Number of times query masking rules was successfully matched.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_ReplicatedPartFetches
metrics.description: Number of times a data part was downloaded from replica of a ReplicatedMergeTree table.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_ReplicatedPartFailedFetches
metrics.description: Number of times a data part was failed to download from replica of a ReplicatedMergeTree table.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_ObsoleteReplicatedParts
metrics.description: Number of times a data part was covered by another data part that has been fetched from a replica (so, we have marked a covered data part as obsolete and no longer needed).

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_ReplicatedPartMerges
metrics.description: Number of times data parts of ReplicatedMergeTree tables were successfully merged.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_ReplicatedPartFetchesOfMerged
metrics.description: Number of times we prefer to download already merged part from replica of ReplicatedMergeTree table instead of performing a merge ourself (usually we prefer doing a merge ourself to save network traffic). This happens when we have not all source parts to perform a merge or when the data part is old enough.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_ReplicatedPartMutations
metrics.description: Number of times data parts of ReplicatedMergeTree tables were successfully mutated.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_ReplicatedPartChecks
metrics.description: Number of times we had to perform advanced search for a data part on replicas or to clarify the need of an existing data part.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_ReplicatedPartChecksFailed
metrics.description: Number of times the advanced search for a data part on replicas did not give result or when unexpected part has been found and moved away.

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_ReplicatedDataLoss

metrics.name: ClickHouseProfileEvents_DataAfterMergeDiffersFromReplica
metrics.description: Number of times data after merge is not byte-identical to the data on another replicas. There could be several reasons: 1. Using newer version of compression library after server update. 2. Using another compression method. 3. Non-deterministic compression algorithm (highly unlikely). 4. Non-deterministic merge algorithm due to logical error in code. 5. Data corruption in memory due to bug in code. 6. Data corruption in memory due to hardware issue. 7. Manual modification of source data after server startup. 8. Manual modification of checksums stored in ZooKeeper. 9. Part format related settings like 'enable_mixed_granularity_parts' are different on different replicas. The server successfully detected this situation and will download merged part from the replica to force the byte-identical result.

FROM signoz_metrics.distributed_time_series_v4_1day
WHERE metric_name = 'ClickHouseMetrics_VersionInteger' and __normalized=false 
GROUP BY `host.name`
